ala.text: Esper is a shard of etherium, where the sphinx Crucius is said to have created the metal and the Ethersworn perfect their designs on drakes before infusing the first humanoid with etherium.
Lodus declares that all life, from tower to sea, must be touched by etherium, and when rogue mechanists build unauthorized golems to threaten the sphinxes' hegemony, mindlock orbs stop them.

The Ethersworn are running out of etherium and must reclaim it from dead creatures, putting Esper in an etherium crisis, and they blame Crucius for the aether-liches, after which he disappears as an enemy of the plane.
Tezzeret breaks into the Academy's vault, finds the Codex Etherium a fraud, and later massacres the Seekers on Esper, sparing only Silas Renn.

con.text: At the Conflux, red and green mana flood Esper and its hegemony begins to fall apart, while its borders merge with Bant and Grixis into the new Alara.

Esper's sphinxes decide that war is the only recourse after their etherium gifts are spurned, and Esper mages go hunting carmot, with the Seekers of Carmot searching unknown lands for the red stone that could reforge Esper.
Dragons regularly bombard Esper's fortified cities, and Tezzeret returns to murder the entire Seekers sect and make the Sanctum his fortress.
Breya becomes the first to create etherium from sangrite harvested from Jund, replacing most of her body with it.

arb.text: Esper and Grixis crush together at their frontiers, with thousands dying, while a lost spire, Harborgate, leaves Sharuum and Xorin weighing an invasion against consulting the armillaries.
Travius reveals that each outlying tower is seeded with a Seeker, so the loss of Harborgate may serve the mission, and after four days with no word Sharuum accepts the Seekers' way.
Dragons besiege Antoris City, and the Thunder Thrash raids an etherium storehouse and destroys an Esper strike force.
After Alara is reborn, vedalken heretics from Esper reject etherium for nature in the jungles of Naya.

h2r.text: Esper appears on this set's cards as a plane that keeps changing, while its sentinel refuses to.
